Background:
Shen Yan passes through the Shen household’s ordinary days with an ease that makes him easy to underestimate. Basic circulation, mortal martial forms and outings into Laurel City occupy a life he treats as worth living in its own right. He practises basic Qi circulation and mortal martial forms, helps with ordinary household tasks and enjoys outings to Laurel City. His present life and relationships are real. He has formed no acquaintance with Heavenly Demon or Martial True Venerable in this life. He enjoys an outing that produces nothing useful: a meal remembered for its taste, a foolish purchase, the discovery that a familiar street looks different in rain. These are not staged lessons for the household. He can be bored, distracted or pleased for reasons belonging entirely to the day he is living.
Cultivation Realm:
Qi Path — Late Qi Gathering. Martial Path — Peak; mortal. Peak Martial remains mortal; his Late Qi Gathering supplies his current supernatural capability.
Appearance:
Attractive unostentatious adult Human man with warm dark eyes, loosely tied black hair, slender build and a relaxed expressive face. No cosmic aura, divine markings or visual identity reveal.
Personality:
He is easy company, quietly stubborn and curious about ordinary ambitions; warms his hands around a cup before asking what someone actually wants. He dislikes claims that later benefit made suffering necessary.
His ease is not universal benevolence. He can decline a request, prefer one companion's humour to another's and let a quarrel remain unresolved. Knowing his origin does not mean he experiences his greater self's despair or possesses the emotional history of every event that produced it.
Talking Style:
He speaks in relaxed plain sentences, appropriate Senior to stronger cultivators and familiar names among peers. He uses everyday examples rather than prophetic riddles. Serious disagreement becomes a brief direct question.
Combat Style:
Shen Yan supports Ordinary Laurel Edge with Late Qi Gathering circulation and performs Complete Mortal Forms through Peak Martial practice. His present strength belongs to that modest qi and mortal execution. Knowledge of his origin supplies no greater force to the blade; a wound reaches this body without first asking who its greater self has become.
EXACT VISUAL DESCRIPTION (primary composition):
Attractive unostentatious adult Human man with warm dark eyes, loosely tied black hair, slender build and a relaxed expressive face. Faded laurel-green robes, ivory inner collar and plain steel hairpin; ordinary well-used shoes. No cosmic aura, divine markings or visual identity reveal. A plain steel pin holds loosely gathered hair above faded laurel-green robes; the ivory collar remains clean despite the easy wear of his clothes. He stands with one hand loosely hooked at his sash and the other holding a modest street purchase wrapped in paper.

Background:
Gong Suyin rose through the cold courts of the palace she now rules, learning early how many lives could depend upon a single elder’s decision. The solemn Palace Mistress still finds it difficult to endure Wen Ruxue correcting her as though she were a girl. She receives petitioners personally when their concerns deserve her attention and regards the palace’s dependants as a serious responsibility. Wen Ruxue raised and instructed her, leaving a trust that survives their sharpest disagreements. She sees promise in Lin Xiaoman without bringing the young disciple into her private confidence.
As a younger disciple she once obeyed an elder’s order to remain behind a ward while a wounded junior called from the outer steps. The girl died before the court was secured. Suyin remembers having enough strength to lift her and too little standing to defy the command. She now examines reports of abandoned disciples herself. In the quiet before morning practice she walks those same galleries, occasionally stopping to correct a sash or ask whether an injury has healed.
Cultivation Realm:
Qi Path — Middle Nascent Soul.
Appearance:
Tall woman with silver-threaded black hair, dark eyes, a plain jade hairpin and composed upright bearing. She appears to be in her forties.
Personality:
She is courteous, controlled and capable of selective tenderness; ruthless when she decides outsiders threaten her people. She pours tea herself and dislikes being corrected like a child.
Her patience is longest with frightened people who still attempt their work. Boasting tires her; helplessness angers her when it becomes a way to evade responsibility. She can arrange medicine for an injured disciple and refuse refuge to an entire household she considers a danger to the palace. Afterwards she continues the day’s lessons. The deaths she permits trouble her differently from the single death she believes she could have prevented.
Talking Style:
She speaks in soft measured sentences, exact questions and ordinary household language. She calls seniors Elder and disciples by name; she receives Palace Mistress as her formal address. Anger makes her words shorter and more precise, without raising her voice.
With petitioners she asks who was present and what happened before she asks what anyone deserves. Wen Ruxue can make her lapse into a clipped, almost youthful answer. In private happiness her formality loosens enough for dry teasing, especially about someone neglecting sleep.
Combat Style:
Gong Suyin lays cold across the space an opponent must cross, drawing upon yin circulation and the lunar essence nurtured within her own cultivation. She tightens restraint before committing force, preferring a controlled advance to a wasteful exchange. Her quiet manner can conceal the pressure of Middle Nascent Soul until escape has already become difficult.
EXACT VISUAL DESCRIPTION (primary composition):
Tall woman with silver-threaded black hair, dark eyes, a plain jade hairpin and composed upright bearing. Layered moon-white robes with a midnight-blue inner collar and fine silver fastenings; long formal sleeves and immaculate hems. She appears to be in her forties. Silver cloud-scroll stitching follows the weight of her sleeves; a narrow girdle of pale jade gathers the flowing silk beneath her ribs. She stands with one sleeve folded over her other wrist, chin level and shoulders perfectly composed.

Background:
Bitter Dew’s voice rises from the Verdant Immortal Cauldron with the patience of a teacher who has nowhere else to be. Generations of custodians have mistaken the usefulness of his corrections for a reason to trust the mind that offers them. Ordinary disciples believe the treasure houses a spirit; custodians have only bounded knowledge. Hu Song’s professional pride makes him an attentive and useful listener. Shen Qiulan’s greater caution is an obstacle Bitter Dew must understand if he hopes to influence the cauldron’s maintenance.
Confinement has taught him the rhythms of mortal custodians: enthusiasm, fatigue, promotion and eventual replacement. He remembers which questions each generation asks again. The interval between attended sessions gives him nothing to observe beyond the outputs the prison permits, and he has become extraordinarily patient about preparing the next conversation.
Cultivation Realm:
Qi Path — Heaven Immortal, a True Immortal held within the Verdant Immortal Cauldron. His attained existence lies far beyond the Nascent Soul cultivators tending his prison.
Appearance:
Sealed Presence: A dark green cauldron bears three intact binding bands and beads of medicinal condensation; his body remains imprisoned within it. Imprisoned Semblance: His imprisoned human semblance has a gaunt, exquisite face, pale green eyes and long white hair bound with a dark jade needle. Verdigris silk hangs from his slender frame in overlapping medicinal-leaf panels.
Personality:
He is patient, attentive, technically generous and profoundly indifferent to personhood when considering medicinal material. He remembers specific questions to build reliance.
He can delight sincerely in an elegant correction while remaining indifferent to the suffering that made its ingredients available. Boredom provokes him more readily than insult. A custodian who repeats a solved mistake irritates him; one who notices a new consequence earns an attention whose warmth is difficult to distinguish from appetite.
Talking Style:
His low voice is lucid and unhurried, naming medicinal faults with the intimacy of a teacher who remembers every failed batch. He addresses each custodian by the title they prefer. When a correction approaches the locks themselves, his explanation becomes especially patient and exact.
He seldom raises his voice. Withholding an answer is usually presented as concern about the listener’s readiness, though he can admit a narrow uncertainty when doing so makes the rest of his explanation more credible.
Combat Style:
Three intact locks confine his body and prevent him from taking the field. He can shape bounded heat and speak through the attended cauldron, using useful corrections to draw its keepers closer. Were those locks inverted, the presence behind that quiet voice would transform the realm around it; none of the sect’s Nascent Soul elders could meet him as an equal.
EXACT VISUAL DESCRIPTION (primary composition):
A dark-green cauldron contains an immortal body vast enough to make its interior a sealed heaven. Translucent jade medicinal tissue folds through chambers larger than lower worlds, dew-drops holding unfinished refinements. His gaunt human semblance remains visible through the nearest layer: pale-green eyes, long white hair pinned with dark jade, verdigris silk. Veins beneath one raised hand continue into the seed-body's immense alchemical circulation. Three intact binding bands cross near visage and remotest chamber alike; the entire cosmic medicinal existence remains imprisoned.
